seams.reason: the commit layer's input seam: the message files (COMMIT_EDITMSG, commit.template), the notes a notes merge leaves to resolve and the targets of the working tree's symbolic links, each held to a limit named there; everything else in commits, notes and stashes parses the bytes it hands back
the password database asked for a user's home (getpwnam_r), the one call std's checked layer does not give the configuration

the diff layer's input seam: the order file diff.orderFile names and the working-tree copy a filter writes out for an external diff, each held to a limit named there; the rest of the diff layer parses the bytes it hands back

discovery's input seam: a candidate git directory's HEAD (file or link target), commondir and a .git file's first byte, each read into a buffer the size of a limit named there; the rest of discovery parses the bytes it hands back
fast-import and fast-export's input seam for the marks files they read, held to the limit named there; the rest of the layer parses the bytes it hands back

the file layer's input seam: a file's contents (whole, stat-measured, or a secret), a lock's pid record and a link's target enter here, each held to the byte limit its caller names, git's 32-byte pid record, or a path's maximum length

the file layer's platform calls std.Io does not give it: the process umask, the effective user, the process id, Windows' CreateHardLinkW, a file's owner checked against the user's token, and NtCreateFile for a handle to a file's attributes alone

SHA-1 on the processor's own instructions: the aarch64 and x86-64 rounds and cpuid as inline assembly, and the feature queries std has no checked form of (Darwin's sysctlbyname, Linux's auxiliary vector)
the hooks' input seam: the first bytes of a hook's file (to know git-lfs's own hook, and a script's #!), each held to a limit named there

relic_lfs's input seam: an object in a store (this repository's, a remote's, a reference directory's, a custom transfer agent's file), a working-tree file a filter cleans and a partial download kept for a resume are read here, a read into a buffer held to the buffer, a whole file to the limit named there, and a stream to the buffer it is read through; everything else in relic_lfs decodes or hashes the bytes it hands back

the maintenance layer's input seam: a gc lock's gc.pid, a rebase's state lines and the server info files, each held to a limit named there; everything else in gc, repack and the server info parses the bytes it hands back
the merge layer's input seam: the conflicted working-tree files rerere reads, held to a limit named there; the rest of the merge layer parses the bytes it hands back

the object layer's input seam: the files it reads (an fsck.skipList, a message given to interpret-trailers), each held to a limit named there; everything else in the layer parses the bytes it hands back

the received pack's bytes enter index-pack here, read back from the temporary pack the stream is copied into, through a reader over a 64 KiB buffer, a positional read held to its caller's end, or a test Io layer's forwarded read into the caller's buffers; every other part of index-pack parses what these return

the pack layer's input seam: a pack file's bytes (read positionally, a block at a time or into a caller's buffer, or mapped), its .idx read whole under Index.OpenOptions.max_bytes, and the object a pack writer takes in, each read held to the limit named there; pack.zig parses the bytes it hands back

the object store's input seam: the files under objects/ the database reads itself (loose objects, pack entries streamed, .keep markers, cruft .mtimes), a whole file held to a limit named there and an object file's reader to the length the object's own header states; the rest of the database parses the bytes it hands back

the patch layer's input seam: the working tree's copy of a path a patch applies to (a file's bytes or a link's target) and the signature file format.signatureFile names, each held to a limit named there; the rest of the patch layer parses the bytes it hands back
the pretty layer's input seam: the rebase and bisect state files a ref listing reads for the branch they name, held to a limit named there; the rest of the pretty layer parses the bytes it hands back
the process layer's input seam: the #! line of a program run on Windows, held to the limit named there

the ref store's input seam: the loose refs and the symbolic links that stand for them, packed-refs and the reftable tables' headers, footers and blocks are read here, each held to a limit named there (a caller's buffer, 256 MiB for a file read whole, a block's most for a table); everything else in the ref store parses the bytes it hands back

the repository layer's input seam: a template's files (held to 1 GiB) and links (held to the platform's longest path), and the index's trailing checksum (held to its fixed size); the rest of the layer takes the bytes it hands back
the kernel's name on FreeBSD (the kern.ostype sysctl), where std has no uname, the one call std's checked layer does not give the repository
the history walks' input seam: a bisect's state files and a mailmap, each held to a limit named there; the rest of the layer parses the bytes it hands back

the transport's input seam: the files the push, the fetch and their serving read whole (a bundle list, a test's records), each held to a limit named there, and the readers over what a hook or pack-objects writes and over a bundle, a downloaded pack or a served repository file, which pkt-line, the bundle header and the pack indexer parse; nothing else in the transport reads a file or a pipe
the walk layer's input seam: the shallow file's contents enter here, held to the limit named there; shallow.zig parses the bytes it hands back

the wire layer's input seam: what a server, a helper program or a credential daemon says (the readers over a program's output and error output and over a socket) and the files the wire reads (a cookie jar, a credential store's file, a pinned key, held to a limit named there) enter here; everything else in the wire parses what it hands back, each read bounded by its parser
